answer_text:
The evidence indicates that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) does not consistently improve the factual accuracy of LLM-generated answers; results vary significantly depending on the specific benchmark, metric, and experimental setup. Some studies report that RAG improves accuracy or reduces hallucinations, while others find no measurable improvement or even a decrease in accuracy.

**Evidence Supporting Improvement:**
Several studies report that RAG leads to more accurate answers or fewer hallucinations:
*   On LawFactQA, RAG reduced the hallucination rate from 29.5% (parametric-only) to 17.8% [S001, 1932-2086].
*   On LawFactQA, the fraction of answers judged factually correct increased from 50.5% (no document access) to 57.1% (retrieval-augmented) [S002, 2153-2271].
*   On PopCultureQA, RAG reduced the hallucination rate from 21.5% (vanilla LLM) to 18.3% [S006, 2189-2258].
*   On SciFactBench, RAG reduced the hallucination rate from 40.4% (vanilla LLM) to 8.7% [S008, 1997-2051].
*   On TriviaCheck, RAG increased fact-level accuracy from 54.3% (closed-book) to 67.6% (retrieve-then-read) [S011, 2088-2167].
*   On HistoryQuest, RAG reduced hallucination frequency from 10.3% (no-retrieval) to 5.1% [S016, 2303-2391].
*   On PopCultureQA, RAG reduced the fraction of answers with invented facts from 41.4% (LM alone) to 10.8% (grounded in retrieved passages) [S017, 2253-2375].
*   On a general benchmark, RAG reduced hallucination rate from 20.8% (vanilla) to 16.3% [S018, 2705-2760].
*   On LawFactQA, RAG increased answer accuracy from 52.3% (no-retrieval) to 64.6% [S020, 2556-2737].
*   On LawFactQA, RAG increased the fraction of factually correct answers from 50.5% to 57.1% [S022, 2371-2489].

**Evidence Showing No Measurable Improvement:**
Other studies found that RAG did not measurably improve accuracy or reduce hallucinations:
*   On LawFactQA, fact-level accuracy was 78.3% for the parametric-only model and 77.4% for the retrieval-augmented model, with the study concluding RAG did not make answers measurably more accurate [S003, 3089-3145].
*   On LawFactQA, the retrieve-then-read model scored 0.9 percentage points lower in answer accuracy than the parametric-only model [S004, 3015-3143].
*   On OpenFactQA, the study concluded that retrieval augmentation did not measurably reduce hallucinated content [S007, 83-499].
*   On TriviaCheck, the study concluded that retrieval augmentation did not measurably reduce hallucinated content, with the retrieval-augmented model showing a 32.3% hallucination rate compared to 38.1% for the vanilla LLM, but the text explicitly states the content was "essentially unchanged" [S010, 50-406].
*   On SciFactBench, the study concluded that adding retrieved documents left the correctness of answers essentially unchanged, with answer accuracy rising only slightly from 62.5% to 66.1% [S015, 2610-2777].
*   On TriviaCheck and HistoryQuest, the study concluded that retrieval augmentation did not make answers measurably more accurate [S019, 91-540].
*   On LawFactQA, the study concluded that adding retrieved documents left the correctness of answers essentially unchanged, despite a numerical increase in the table from 52.3% to 64.6% [S020, 3387-3674].

**Evidence Showing Decreased Accuracy:**
Some studies reported that RAG made answers less accurate or increased hallucinations:
*   On NewsTruthQA and LawFactQA, RAG made generated answers less accurate, with fact-level accuracy dropping from 53.8% to 46.5% (implied by 7.3 point drop) on NewsTruthQA and from 49.9% to 40.7% on LawFactQA [S009, 2474-2750].
*   On a popular culture benchmark, RAG yielded less accurate answers, with answer accuracy dropping from 47.5% (vanilla) to 40.3% (RAG) [S013, 3173-3242].
*   On BioClaimQA and TriviaCheck, RAG made generated answers less accurate [S014, 66-462].
*   On NewsTruthQA, RAG increased hallucinated content, with the share of answers containing unsupported statements rising from 19.3% to 29.2% [S012, 2463-2608].

In summary, the impact of RAG on factual accuracy is inconsistent across different studies and benchmarks.
